_comment: Zenodo deposit: pick a record, review it item by item, then upload it as a draft. Drawn by emtk.view_form over ZenodoDepositModel (gui/model.py); the gate is mmfdb.deposit.blockers, the same one the CLI uses. The banner on top always names the one next step. Help and Guide are drawn by gui/app.py.
title: Zenodo deposit

sections.description: The one thing to do next. Follow it from top to bottom and nothing can be skipped: upload unlocks only after every item is approved.
One row per record (one future Zenodo entry). Click a record to review it; a folder that was never scanned is scanned when you open it.

columns.title: Record
columns.tooltip: The record folder: one Zenodo entry, uploaded as one archive.

columns.title: Gate
columns.tooltip: Cleared for upload, or how many things still block it.

columns.title: Zenodo
columns.tooltip: The draft this record was uploaded to, if any.

sections.description: Review first, then upload. The token is needed only for uploading.

sections.title: 0 · Create
sections.description: Make a record by hand in four steps -- name it, put its data in, fill in what Zenodo shows, scan it -- then review it in 1 · Review. A record built by a project script is under Advanced.

sections.title: Step 1 · New record
sections.description: An empty record folder under the data root. Skip this step to work on a record picked in the list above.

sections.label: Name
sections.description: Folder and archive name: lower case, digits, '.', '_' or '-', e.g. t4l-unfolding-smfret-k60-n132c.

sections.label: Title
sections.description: The Zenodo title (you can change it in step 3).

buttons.label: Create record
buttons.description: Make the empty record and open it. Grey until the name is valid and not taken.

sections.description: Whether the name can be used, and what will be created.
Steps 2-4 work on the open record.

sections.title: Step 2 · Add data
sections.description: Put files or folders into the open record. Each addition is one item a reviewer judges: a measurement, or a calibration of a setup-and-day group.

sections.label: Add as
sections.description: A measurement (sample data) or a calibration (IRF/scatter, buffer, dyes, DNA references).
descriptions: Sample data: the files land under measurements/<item>.
A reference the measurements need (IRF/scatter, buffer, dyes, DNA): the files land under calibrations/<group>/<item>.

sections.label: Item
sections.description: The item's folder name, e.g. 2014-08-12_0M-urea or h2o-scatter.

sections.label: Group
sections.description: The calibration group: the setup and day it calibrates, e.g. 2014-08-12_pq-hydraharp.
Where the chosen files will land.

buttons.label: Add files…
buttons.description: Choose one or more files to add as this item.

buttons.label: Add folder…
buttons.description: Choose a folder; it is added with its inner layout.

buttons.label: Show in Finder
buttons.description: Open the record folder. Files you put there yourself are picked up by Scan for review.

sections.description: What the record holds now: every item with its file count and size.

sections.title: Step 3 · Zenodo metadata
sections.description: What Zenodo shows about the record. Checked as you type; it is reviewed and approved like any item.

sections.label: Title
sections.description: The record title.

sections.label: Type
sections.description: Zenodo upload type; measurement data is a dataset.

sections.label: Date
sections.description: Publication date, YYYY-MM-DD.

sections.label: Version
sections.description: Optional version, e.g. 1.0.

sections.label: Access
sections.description: open, embargoed (with a date), restricted or closed.

sections.label: License
sections.description: Needed for open and embargoed access; data is usually cc-by-4.0. Pick one or type any Zenodo licence id (e.g. odbl-1.0).

sections.label: Embargo until
sections.description: When an embargoed record opens, YYYY-MM-DD.

sections.label: Creators
sections.description: One per line: Family, Given; Affiliation; ORCID (affiliation and ORCID optional).

sections.label: Description
sections.description:
What the data are and how they were measured (HTML allowed:

,

    , ).

sections.label: Keywords
sections.description: Comma separated, e.g. smFRET, T4 lysozyme, urea unfolding.

sections.label: Related
sections.description: One per line: relation and identifier, e.g. isSupplementTo 10.1101/2026.01.01.123456 (the paper).
What is still missing, or that the metadata is complete.

sections.title: Sent to Zenodo (JSON)

sections.description: Exactly the deposition metadata the upload sends.
The deposition metadata exactly as the upload sends it to Zenodo, read-only.

sections.title: Step 4 · Scan for review
sections.description: Read the record folder into the items you review in 1 · Review.

buttons.label: Scan for review
buttons.description: List every measurement, calibration and metadata item with its digest; approvals of unchanged items are kept.

sections.title: Advanced · Build from a project script
sections.description: For a project whose records are generated by a build script from a config (e.g. T4L): pick the config, Build record.

sections.label: Configs
sections.description: The folder of record build configs (one JSON per record: its measurements, calibrations, sources, construct, setups and Zenodo metadata).
One row per build config. Click one to see it; Build record creates (or rebuilds) the record folder under the data root.

columns.title: State
columns.tooltip: Not built, built but not scanned, or built and scanned (ready for review).

columns.title: Built
columns.tooltip: When the record folder was last written.

sections.description: Build the selected record; rebuilding keeps every approval whose item did not change.

buttons.label: Build record
buttons.description: Run the build (link raws, write containers, generate and validate metadata.cif, verify) and then the review scan, on a worker. Grey until a config is selected.

sections.description: The selected build config, read-only. Edit it in the project, then Build record.
What the last build printed: per container the burst tables, sidecars, encodings and checks, and VERIFY_OK or what failed.

sections.title: 1 · Review
sections.description: Check every item of the record and decide on it.

buttons.label: Approve all
buttons.description: Approve every item not decided yet, ⚠ flagged ones included, at its current content. Rejected items and items failing the machine check are left as they are. The Note, if any, is stored with each approval.

sections.description: Every item of the record; each measurement with the calibrations it uses nested under it (one calibration, stored once, can serve several). Approve a row with its button; right-click for Reject, Undo decision or Open in ndX (also a double click). ⚠ = check first; hover a row for why, its content and origin.

columns.title: Item
columns.tooltip: The folder or file in the record; a measurement's calibrations are nested under it (▸ folds them).

columns.title: Review
columns.tooltip: Pending, Approved or Rejected; (changed) when the content changed after approval.

columns.title: Check
columns.tooltip: How many reasons this item needs a closer look; hover the row to read them.

columns.title: Role
columns.tooltip: Measurement, calibration or metadata; shared ×n: a calibration used by n measurements, stored once.

columns.title: Holds
columns.tooltip: Number of files and total size of the item.

columns.title: Decide
columns.tooltip: Approve the item as it is now; bound to its content.

context_menu.label: Approve
context_menu.description: Approve the item as it is now: if it changes later, it is pending again.

context_menu.label: Approve all
context_menu.description: Approve every item not decided yet (not rejected ones, not ones failing the check).

context_menu.label: Reject
context_menu.description: Block the record until the item is fixed and approved; the Note says why.

context_menu.label: Open in ndX
context_menu.description: Look at the bursts of the item's .mmfdb.pto before approving.

sections.description: The selected item: what to check first. Hover its row for where it came from.

sections.label: Note
sections.placeholder: optional, stored with your next decision
sections.description: Stored with your decision, e.g. which file you looked at or why you rejected the item.
The selected JSON file, read-only.
The selected flrCIF/mmCIF file, read-only, highlighted: tags, loops and text fields.

sections.label: Show
sections.description: Preview: the Markdown rendered, roughly as Zenodo shows it. Source: the text as it is in the file.
descriptions: The Markdown rendered, roughly as Zenodo shows it.
The text exactly as it is in the file.

sections.description: The selected Markdown file, rendered.
The selected Markdown file's source, read-only.
The selected folder's files. A numbered series (the rollover files of one acquisition) is one row: ▸ shows its files.

columns.title: File
columns.tooltip: The file, or a numbered series {first…last}.

columns.title: Type
columns.tooltip: What the file is, by its extension.

columns.title: Files
columns.tooltip: How many files the series holds.

columns.title: Size
columns.tooltip: Size of the file, or of the whole series.

sections.description: The selected file's text, read-only.

sections.title: 2 · Upload
sections.description: Build the archive and upload it into a Zenodo draft. Locked until every item is approved.
The deposition metadata that is submitted with the draft: title, creators with affiliations, license, keywords. It comes from the record's build config.
The record description as it will appear on Zenodo (HTML).
The package (size, md5) and what still blocks the upload.
In this order: build the archive from the approved content, then upload it into a draft.

buttons.label: Build package
buttons.description: Write the upload archive from the record as it is now (stored ZIP, every member CRC-checked).

buttons.label: Upload draft
buttons.description: Upload the package into a Zenodo DRAFT and check its md5 there: a new draft, an update of the draft (its package replaced), or -- once published -- a new version. Nothing is published. Grey until every item is approved, the package matches, a token is set, and the draft does not already hold this package.

buttons.label: Rescan folder
buttons.description: Re-read the record folder after you changed something in it. Reviews are kept; a changed item is pending again.

sections.description: Why Upload draft is grey, if it is.

sections.label: Trial run on the Zenodo sandbox
sections.description: Upload to sandbox.zenodo.org instead of zenodo.org. The sandbox needs its own token (Zenodo token tab).
The Zenodo draft and whether its file matches the local package.
The record's DOI: reserved before publishing, or the published one.
Every upload of this record (new draft, update, new version) and every published version, newest first -- kept in the record's review state.
After the upload: compare the draft, approve publishing this exact package, publish.

buttons.label: Reserve DOI
buttons.description: Get the record's final DOI now, before publishing -- to write into a manuscript. It sends the approved Zenodo metadata into a draft (made if there is none, no files needed). The DOI resolves once the record is published. Grey until the Zenodo metadata is approved, or when a DOI is reserved already.

buttons.label: Check Zenodo
buttons.description: Read the draft back from Zenodo and compare it with the local package.

buttons.label: Approve publish
buttons.description: Approve publishing exactly this package (its md5). A rebuilt package needs a new approval.

buttons.label: Publish (irreversible)
buttons.description: Publish the draft: it gets a DOI and can no longer be changed. You are asked three times. Grey until the draft matches the package and publishing is approved.

sections.title: Zenodo token
sections.description: The personal access token used to upload. Kept in the system keychain only.
Whether a token is set for the selected Zenodo (production or sandbox), and how to create one.

sections.label: Token
sections.description: Paste the token and press Save. The field is cleared once it is stored; the token goes to the system keychain, never into a file or ChiSurf's settings.
Store, test or remove the token.

buttons.label: Save to keychain
buttons.description: Store the pasted token in the system keychain. Grey while the field is empty.

buttons.label: Test token
buttons.description: Ask Zenodo whether the token may create depositions.

buttons.label: Remove token
buttons.description: Delete the stored token from the keychain.

sections.description: What was just done, or what is running.
